description: When the Mixer 01 of the E.C.M INCIMMET S.A, moved by the positive south ramp, with direction to surface (Unicon concrete plant), at the height of the 3630 (Before 440), the operator observes that untimely lights and the engine go off, the control controls do not respond and the equipment starts to reverse. At 3 meters the operator jumps out of the cabin and at 20 meters the team hits the right gable and turns to its side left. In the area, in the circumstances of the event there was no presence of personnel or equipment that could have been affected.
sif_reason: This is a serious loss-of-control event: a concrete mixer truck suffered an electrical/engine failure on a ramp (lights and engine cutting out, controls becoming unresponsive), causing the vehicle to begin uncontrolled reverse travel on an incline. The operator made the decision to jump from the moving cabin at 3 meters of travel — jumping from a moving vehicle is itself a high-risk action with real potential for serious fall/impact injury, independent of the vehicle's subsequent crash. The unmanned vehicle then continued for approximately 20 meters, struck the right gable, and rolled/turned onto its left side. This combines multiple high-energy mechanisms: (1) an uncontrolled heavy-vehicle runaway on a ramp, (2) an operator jumping from a moving vehicle, and (3) a resulting vehicle collision and rollover. The only reason this did not result in injury appears to be fortunate circumstances (no personnel/equipment in the path, and the operator's jump not resulting in an injury as described) rather than an effective engineered control.
evidence_text: "the operator observes that untimely lights and the engine go off, the control controls do not respond and the equipment starts to reverse. At 3 meters the operator jumps out of the cabin and at 20 meters the team hits the right gable and turns to its side left"
hazard_notes: Combined mechanical/gravitational — uncontrolled heavy vehicle (concrete mixer) runaway on a ramp due to sudden loss of engine/electrical control, operator jumping from a moving vehicle, and subsequent vehicle collision with a fixed structure resulting in rollover
consequence_notes: Under a worse-case variation of this same event (operator jumping at higher speed or less favorable body position, landing on hard/uneven ground, being run over by the reversing vehicle, or personnel/other equipment being present in the runaway's path or at the point of collision/rollover), this could plausibly result in fatality or severe crush/impact trauma — this is a hazard category with an inherently high severity ceiling, and the described outcome (no injury, no personnel present) reflects a fortunate variation rather than an effective control
barrier_notes: Failed — the vehicle's engine/electrical/control system failed unexpectedly, and there is no indication of a functioning parking brake, runaway-vehicle arrestor, or fail-safe braking system that should have prevented an uncontrolled reverse roll on a ramp; the absence of personnel/equipment in the runaway path was circumstantial, not the result of an engineered exclusion zone or traffic control measure
exposure_notes: Operator physically present in the cabin during the loss of control and reversing runaway, then exposed to fall/impact risk while jumping from the moving vehicle; broader area (ramp/roadway) exposed to an unmanned, uncontrolled 20-meter runaway that ended in collision and rollover — the narrative notes no personnel/equipment were in that path on this occasion

description: In tower N ° 6 of the old 50 KV LT (disabled and de-energized and 90% disassembled) located in the city of Pasco, the cutting of the last profiles of the base of the tower previously disassembled was carried out, using oxyfuel equipment, at 11:45 a.m., the safety supervisor of Proingcom and the foreman, who were in the external part of the fenced area supervising the activity, indicate the paralysis of activities and evacuation to the refuge due to the orange alert indicated on the detector of storms. During the evacuation of the last 02 employees who were inside the fenced area, a loud sound was heard, provoking a scare, which caused the staff to throw themselves to the floor within the area, then proceeded to leave the work area by their own means through the staircase. Apparently the loud sound would correspond to an electrical discharge in the cable guard that passes over the old towers.
sif_reason: The event involved a potential high-energy electrical discharge near workers during evacuation. Although the old 50 kV line was reported as de-energized, an electrical discharge was apparently heard from an overhead cable guard, creating a credible electrical shock/arc hazard.
evidence_text: During evacuation due to a storm alert, a loud sound apparently corresponding to an electrical discharge was heard from the cable guard passing over the old towers. Two employees were still inside the fenced area at the time.
hazard_notes: Electrical energy / electrical discharge from an overhead cable associated with a 50 kV installation.
consequence_notes: Severe electrical shock, arc-related burns, electrocution, or fatality.
barrier_notes: The system was reported as disabled, de-energized, and 90% dismantled, and activities were stopped with evacuation ordered after the storm alert. However, the reported electrical discharge indicates that electrical hazards were still potentially present.
exposure_notes: Two workers were inside the fenced work area near the old electrical infrastructure during the suspected discharge.
